session_policy.notes: Begin from the learner's best available explanation language, then teach the selected target. Rich kinship-language culture/usage teaching requires the researched Tier 1 or Tier 2 target profile. Every Tier 3 target still has the same 14 broad relationship concepts for comparison and recognition-safe Games.

rules.notes: Resolve the actual relationship first: parent, child, sibling, grandparent, aunt/uncle, cousin, niece/nephew, partner/spouse, and so on. Then choose the target language's term.

A target language may lexicalize dimensions that the learner's source language leaves implicit, including relative age, gender, maternal/paternal side, generation, marriage link, or speaker-relative status.

Reference forms, address forms, honorific forms, affectionate forms, and community usage can differ. Teach the neutral beginner form first and label meaningful alternatives instead of flattening them into one translation.

triggers.notes: Available from the lesson catalog as an A1 vocabulary-and-kinship-language lesson. Tier 1 and Tier 2 targets expose the rich profile; Tier 3 targets expose the comparison/game core.
May be placed early in Tier 1 and Tier 2 language paths where basic personal-description vocabulary is appropriate.

game_exports.notes: The game pairs relationship concepts, not English words. Multiple target forms may be accepted when the language lexicalizes a distinction the prompt has not specified.

presentation.scroll_mode: Render the groups in one short vertical lesson.
presentation.pages_mode: Render each semantic group as one or more pages while preserving source-first then target-second order.
presentation.teacher_presentation_mode: Use the same lesson graph and profile data with classroom-sized controls; do not fork content.
presentation.pairing_policy: Source bridge, reusable support-language facts, rich target profile, and universal game vocabulary are resolved independently. Never generate a source-by-target matrix.
